subject.title: Add testing framework for cron jobs and skills (dry-run mode)

question: What side-effect boundary should OpenClaw guarantee for cron and skills dry-run/testing, and should that boundary share a request-scoped contract with global agent dry-run?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the implementation would define a security-sensitive public preview contract across cron, skills, tools, hooks, channels, external APIs, and possible config/CLI surfaces.

options.title: Design One Request-Scoped Contract
options.body: Define cron test/validate, skills test, and shared tool interception semantics together so every preview mode has the same side-effect guarantees.

options.title: Ship Cron-Only Validation First
options.body: Add cron config, schedule, and delivery validation while leaving skill execution and global tool interception to separate follow-up decisions.

options.title: Defer Broad Dry-Run Semantics
options.body: Keep existing command-specific dry-run surfaces until a maintainer sponsors the broader trusted preview boundary.

recommendation.title: Design One Request-Scoped Contract
recommendation.body: Define cron test/validate, skills test, and shared tool interception semantics together so every preview mode has the same side-effect guarantees.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest combined signal from prior issue review plus recent history across cron CLI, skills CLI, Gateway cron, and agent tool-adapter surfaces.
